articles.title: Air traffic chaos and compensation: 'Shutdown cost us more than £1,000'
articles.text:
Catie and Phil Allen should have been enjoying their first holiday in two-and-a-half years. Instead, they are at home ringing round for refunds that won't be paid.

The couple are among the many thousands of air passengers caught up in the chaos caused by the four-hour shutdown of the UK's air traffic control system on Tuesday.

It means their holiday to Slovenia has been cancelled and - although their flight was refunded by British Airways - they estimate being left £1,300 out of pocket from unused accommodation and excursions.

It's not the first time - and won't be the last - when passengers are left flying on a wing and a prayer after problems at UK airports. So, here is how their case relates to others, and why they have taken such a big hit.

Catie, 30, and Phil, 34, were sat on a British Airways flight to Ljubljana on Tuesday that never took off.

If a flight is cancelled, airlines must get customers to their destination as quickly as possible at no extra cost, even if it is with a rival carrier.

Alternatively, passengers can take a refund, which should also be offered for flight delays of more than five hours.

In Catie and Phil's case, the alternative flight offered would not have arrived until Saturday morning - four days into their week-long holiday.

So they took the refund. That was not easy. The chatbot only seemed to allow them to rebook, and it took more than an hour waiting to speak to BA on the phone before the refund was confirmed. It will take a week to be paid.

When airlines are at fault, extra compensation is paid under UK and EU rules. But not this time, because the air traffic control issues were beyond airlines' control. Even so, airlines themselves are furious that they have been saddled with a bill of millions of pounds.

BA also refunded the couple's car hire, which had been organised through the airline. The problem for the couple was that they had booked accommodation and excursions separately, and that is money they have lost.

The hotel stays, booked separately, have their own terms and conditions and cancelling so late meant there were no refunds. One explained to Catie that they were a family business that could not afford to do so.

This is different to package holidays, which are covered in full if a flight is cancelled.

"We feel we are penalised for trying to save money," said Catie, who contacted BBC Your Voice about their situation, although she added that "our problems are very small in the bigger scheme of things".

One excursion was later refunded but - having worked in the aviation sector - Catie is annoyed that the air traffic problem extended so long as to ruin their holiday.

"We have been saving tirelessly for this trip and we have lost over £1,000 with no way of getting it back. And most of all, we've got no holiday to go on, which we've been looking forward to for years," she said.

articles.title: Primark finally set to launch online deliveries
articles.text:
Primark has said it plans to launch a home delivery service in Britain, four years after it made its first foray into e-commerce.

The retailer did not say when it expects to launch the service, but it has bought a warehouse in Sheffield to enable it to ship products to homes.

The company said there was "opportunity for profitable growth" through home deliveries, which could help boost trade after Primark reported subdued sales following the recent hot weather.

Analysts said the decision to offer home delivery after years of resistance - including through the pandemic - indicated that Primark was facing major challenges from ultra-fast-fashion brands such as Shein.

Primark did not sell goods online until 2022, when it launched a click-and-collect service which meant shoppers still had to travel to pick up their purchases.

Associated British Foods (ABF), which owns Primark, said the fashion chain would "continue to grow click and collect and... will in the future offer home delivery in Great Britain".

ABF predicts Primark's UK sales will grow by about 1% in the fourth quarter of the year. But like-for-like sales - a key metric in the retail industry, which strips out the impact of store openings and closures - are expected to be "broadly flat" in the UK, and fall 3% across its global operations.

It said sales of autumn/winter clothing started later than normal due to the hot weather in the summer, but "trading was stronger when the weather cooled towards the end of the quarter".

The fast-fashion chain is struggling to compete with brands such as Shein and Boohoo, as well as alternative platforms such as TikTok Shop and Vinted, and in July said it was lowering prices on hundreds of clothing items.

Retail analyst Julie Palmer said that "Primark has been playing catch up for years" and launching home deliveries "is as much about defence as growth".

She told BBC News that "the real test" for the brand is whether it can make home deliveries profitable at the low prices customers have come to expect from fast fashion chains.

"Shein and Vinted have already reset customer expectations on convenience," she said, adding that a "slick and effective returns policy" will also be key.

ABF is planning to spin off Primark from its food business next year.

articles.title: The one thing you need to do to succeed - according to top bosses
articles.text:
What makes someone stand out in a crowded workplace?

For some bosses, it's less about having the perfect CV and more about the way you think, the questions you ask and whether you're prepared to take a chance.

Six business founders and leaders share the qualities they notice most and the advice they would give to people trying to get ahead.

Charlotte Tilbury says one of the biggest things that has driven her career is refusing to let other people set limits on what she can do.

"Nothing is impossible in life - it's only your own limitations you give yourself."

The beauty mogul says there will always be naysayers, and there were plenty of people who told her she was "mad" or that her ideas would not work but it's important to ignore them.

Tilbury recommends trying not to think of setbacks as mistakes, but as opportunities to rethink and improve.

"I don't think about mistakes, I think mistakes are opportunities," she says.

Many of the biggest challenges she faced ultimately made her a stronger business leader and "challenge is opportunity and it leads you to greater places".

Charlie Bowes-Lyon, co-founder of deodorant brand Wild, says attitude matters far more than having the perfect set of skills.

"For me, it's 90% attitude and 10% skills, as skills can be taught, attitude can't."

One thing he wishes he had realised earlier is that even successful people do not always feel as confident as they appear and "everyone is faking it until they're making it".

If you find yourself at a job interview, Bowes-Lyon says it's really important to have a few questions at the end as "candidates who say they have no questions rarely get the job".

One question he recommends asking the interviewer is what success in the job looks like.

articles.title: Oil, gas and borrowing costs surge as fears over Middle East escalate
articles.text:
The price of oil has jumped to $105 a barrel amid signs the conflict in the Middle East will not be resolved quickly, fuelling fears that inflation could accelerate.

With the conflict between the US and Iran in the Gulf intensifying in recent days, the cost of both crude oil and gas has been rising sharply. Brent crude went back above $100 a barrel on Wednesday and has continued to climb.

The war has led to the effective closure of the Strait of Hormuz, preventing supplies of oil and gas from the Gulf from reaching global markets.

US and UK long-term borrowing costs also surged to their highest level in decades.

Speaking at a Republican Party convention in Texas on Wednesday, President Trump said he did not think the fighting would end until after the US mid-term elections in November.

Analysts said the combination of rising energy costs and higher borrowing costs was adding pressure on financial markets.

Chris Beauchamp, chief market analyst at trading platform IG, said investors were becoming increasingly concerned about the economic impact of higher oil prices.

"It feels like investors worldwide are now waking up to the crisis in oil markets," Beauchamp said. He warned that the surge in energy prices could weigh heavily on the global economy if it continues.

Concerns have also grown after Iran-aligned Houthi forces were reported to have seized Yemen's port of Mokha, a key Red Sea port.

The move could elevate fears of further shipping disruptions.

The price of natural gas has also been soaring on wholesale markets. In the UK, it rose above 200p a therm for the first time since the end of 2022.

Storage levels in Europe are much lower than normal for the time of year, and the need to fill reserves ahead of the winter has helped to push up prices.

articles.title: US consumers faced more high prices in August as Iran war raised energy costs
articles.text:
US consumer prices remained stubbornly high in August as the end of the ceasefire between the US and Iran pushed energy prices up, according to data from the US Bureau of Labor Statistics released on Friday.

The annualized inflation rate was 3.4%, the same as it was in July. The most recent peak was seen in May, when the inflation rate hit a three-year high at 4.2%. Core inflation, which strips out volatile energy and food prices, increased 0.3% from the month before and 2.4% annually.

Gasoline increased 27.4% compared with the year before, accounting for more than one-third of the overall monthly increase in prices. Fuel , which is used to power and heat homes, increased annually at a staggering 52%.

Prices of common grocery store essentials, such as meat, poultry, eggs and dairy, increased slightly, from 0.1% to 0.3%. Lettuce prices continued to fall, probably continued fallout from the cyclosporiasis outbreak.

Despite dipping from its most recent peak, inflation remained above levels that were seen before the war in Iran, largely because of higher energy prices. On Friday, the cost of diesel, used for trucks, buses and trains, rose past $6 a gallon for the first time ever. Brent crude, the international benchmark for oil prices, also surpassed $108 on Friday, its highest level since May. Meanwhile, gas prices at the pump sat at an average of $4.29 a gallon, $1.10 higher than the average a year ago, according to AAA.

It’s a worrying sign for Republicans, who are on the ballot at a time when consumer sentiment has hit record lows and Americans say they are struggling to afford gas and groceries. Concerns over inflation have also bled into the US bond market, where the yields on some US treasurys have reached their highest points since the 2008 recession. Yet it’s unclear when relief will come.

The White House is aware of what this could mean for the upcoming elections. On Wednesday night, Trump said Americans would get a $5,000 “dividend” if Republicans win a majority in the midterms, which critics said was akin to bribery.

One of the most direct ways the federal government can affect prices comes from the power of the US Federal Reserve, which sets the interest rates that have an effect on the price of loans, including mortgages, car payments and student debt.

With prices remaining stubbornly high and core inflation rising, Friday’s report bolsters the likelihood that the Fed will vote to increase rates at its board meeting next week.. Either move could have heavy implications for the US economy.

In a social media post last week, Trump said the central bank “must get smart” and lower rates. “A STRONG COUNTRY MEANS A LOWER INTEREST RATE,” he declared.

But pressure to increase rates has been growing. At the Fed’s last board meeting in July, it voted 9-3 to maintain rates – the first time in a decade that three board members shared dissent over a policy decision.

Historically, raising interest rates helps to lower inflation – making investments more expensive slows the economy. Inflation reached 9.1%, a 40-year high, in 2022. After the Fed spent the next few years increasing interest rates, up to a range of 5.25%-5.5%, inflation went down to 2.3% in April 2025.

Interest rates now sit at a range of 3.5%-3.75%, two percentage points lower than where they were two years ago. With inflation back up, some Fed economists have said it might be time for higher interest rates.

Last week, the Fed governor Christopher Waller said there was “considerable uncertainty about how military conflicts, trade policy, and artificial intelligence will affect prices and economic activity” and it might be appropriate to raise rates if inflation showed no signs of easing.

“If there is continued progress toward our 2% goal, then I am willing to support holding the policy rate at its current level,” he said at a Reuters event. “But if inflation comes in hot, I would consider a rate hike.”

The Fed’s new chair, Kevin Warsh, has made it clear the central bank will combat inflation during his tenure and achieve price stability. During a closely watched speech in Jackson Hole, Wyoming, last month, Warsh said that underlying inflation trends had not “meaningfully improved” over the summer.

“We must be confident that underlying inflation is moving to our objective, clearly and at sufficient speed. Otherwise, we have work to do,” Warsh said.

articles.title: Global bond sell-off resumes as surging oil prices stoke fears about inflation
articles.text:
Nervous investors across big economies have been dumping government bonds, driving up the cost of borrowing, as surging oil prices amplified fears about rising inflation.

The cost of a barrel of oil jumped 6% to above $107 on Thursday amid concerns that advances by Houthi rebels along the Red Sea coast in Yemen could choke off Saudi crude exports.

The global bond sell-off that has rocked markets in recent weeks resumed in response to the news from the Middle East – which came against a backdrop of escalating concern about out-of-control government borrowing.

Higher oil prices, which had already climbed since hostilities resumed in the Iran war, are expected to drive up inflation, prompting central banks to raise interest rates and putting the brakes on economic growth.

Donald Trump suggested on Wednesday that the conflict with Iran could continue until “immediately after” November’s US midterm elections, at which point he claimed oil prices would be “tumbling downward”.

The European Central Bank (ECB) raised its main interest rate to 2.5% on Thursday, with its president, Christine Lagarde, saying: “We believe inflation will be longer lasting than we had anticipated.”

“The conflict in the Middle ​East continues ​to ⁠generate inflation pressures, and inflation is set to ​remain well above target for ​an ⁠extended period,” she added.

As Thursday’s sell-off gathered pace in London, the yield, or interest rate, on 10-year UK government bonds surged above 5.37% – the highest cost of borrowing since 2007 – creating a fresh headache for the new chancellor, John Healey.

With less than seven weeks to go until Healey’s first budget on 28 October, higher interest rates on the UK’s debt-pile will raise the cost of future investment projects and eat into the Treasury’s fiscal headroom.

At the same time, the prospect of higher energy bills as oil and gas prices rise is likely to intensify pressure on the government to help consumers to weather the winter.

Unleaded petrol prices have already risen by 6p a litre since the start of September, according to the motoring organisation the RAC, while the prospect of higher inflation has prompted some banks to raise their mortgage rates.

Healey has promised to provide a “breathing space” for UK households while also addressing the cost of doing business.

In a speech on Monday, however, he also sought to tame bond market fears by committing himself to “controlling borrowing to bear down on inflation, and reducing long-term pressures on our public finances”.

In the US, where Trump has promised to write a $5,000 (£3,700) cheque for every adult citizen if the Republicans win the midterms, Thursday’s sell-off pushed up the yield on 10-year borrowing to 4.92% – the highest since 2023.

The cost of longer-term borrowing also continued to surge, with 30-year yields hitting the highest level since 2007, despite the US treasury secretary, Scott Bessent, intervening directly in debt markets on Wednesday.

Bessent hoped to bring down yields by buying back $6bn worth of government debt; but investors appeared to respond by deepening the sell-off.

Kyle Rodda, a senior financial market analyst at the broker Capital.com, said: “Ultimately, a sustained drop in long-end yields can ​only be achieved by genuine shifts in macroeconomic policy: ​either the US government pulling back on spending or the ​Fed lifting rates.”

Policymakers at the Federal Reserve, the US central bank, will meet under its new chair, Kevin Warsh, to set interest rates next week.

Markets are expecting a rise – potentially enraging Trump, who has repeatedly demanded rate cuts. In a TruthSocial post last week, the president said: “The Fed Board, with its great new leader, must get smart – BE PATRIOTS for a change.”

A plethora of UK data to be published over the next week, including on inflation, jobs and growth, will give an updated snapshot of how resilient the British economy has been in the face of the Iran war.

In the first six months of the year, UK growth was the strongest among the G7 economies. This was despite higher-than-expected oil prices and the absence of hoped-for rate cuts.

Bank of England policymakers will also meet next week, but are expected to leave the UK’s key interest rate on hold at 3.75% for the time being as they continue to monitor the impact of higher oil prices.

articles.title: US Open 2026 results: Alexander Zverev beats Karen Khachanov to reach final
articles.text:
Alexander Zverev beat Karen Khachanov at the US Open to reach a third Grand Slam final in a row and continue his bid for a second major of the year.

The top seed put in a commanding performance to beat the Russian 6-3 7-6 (9-7) 7-6 (8-6).

Germany's Zverev is the favourite in New York after ending his long wait for a Grand Slam title with his French Open triumph in June.

He reached the Wimbledon final in July, losing in four sets to world number one Jannik Sinner.

The 29-year-old will play either eighth seed Ben Shelton or 11th seed Frances Tiafoe in Sunday's showpiece, with the two Americans set to meet in Friday's night session.

"I think it [Sunday] will be incredibly special especially, these two guys are crowd favourites and everyone loves them," said Zverev.

"Tonight will be an epic semi-final and I am looking forward to watching it. Hopefully I can not make their American dream come true."

With Sinner and defending US Open champion Carlos Alcaraz suffering with injuries this year, Zverev has found a consistency that has allowed him to reach all four Grand Slam semi-finals.

He started off the tournament in New York slowly, being taken to five sets in his opening two matches, but has not dropped a set since.

Zverev faced brief moments of pressure against world number 50 Khachanov, saving two set points in the third set, but otherwise remained in control.

"After the second round, at about 3am I was sitting with my team in the locker room and we were laughing at how bad I was playing," Zverev said.

"That sense of humour helped me. I obviously have improved a bit otherwise I would not be in the US Open final."

Zverev won 13 of 15 points behind his first serve and all nine points at the net in the first set as he broke Khachanov to go 5-3 up before serving out the opener.

Khachanov fought back after going a break down early in the second set and forced a tie-break, saving set point with a magnificent backhand to polish off a 22-shot rally.

In a pivotal point of the match, it was Zverev who took the initiative to earn another set point, converting it as he outlasted Khachanov in a draining rally with some magnificent defence from the baseline.

In the third set, both players remained on serve without conceding a single break point to reach another tie-break.

It was Khachanov who settled quickest into the tie-break, opening up a lead and creating two set points - both of which were saved by Zverev.

From there the top seed never looked back, ultimately clinching victory as Khachanov put a forehand long.

After reaching his sixth major final, Zverev stood arms wide in celebration facing his coaching team, before going to the net to shake hands with Khachanov.

Victory means Zverev is into his second US Open final after suffering a heartbreaking five-set loss to Dominic Thiem in 2020.

articles.title: Razaullah: 'Razball' reigns as Pakistan thrive in chaos against England on day three at Edgbaston
articles.text:
Cancel the tee time at the Belfry, rearrange the trip to Cadbury World and abort the shopping jolly to the Bullring.

The reason? Pakistan's new star Razaullah and 'Razball'.

England's bowlers were thwarted by a Pakistan side who mixed batting belligerence with brilliance and instead of a Saturday off must reconvene at Edgbaston for day four.

The brilliance was provided by Razaullah, who produced a dizzying knock to breathe life into the third Test and lift the spirits of Pakistan supporters everywhere. A new hero, a new hope.

Bazball might be on its way out, but Birmingham might just have witnessed the birth of a new phenomenon during two hours of unbridled chaos where the Test debutant made a stunning 81 off 63 balls coming in at number nine.

A raw 21-year-old with just eight first-class matches to his name, selected more as a tearaway fast bowler reminiscent of Waqar Younis, Razaullah was probably not a name on the radar of England's bowlers when he was called up amid wholesale changes made by Pakistan before the final Test.

After some blistering strokeplay when he took down the home side's attack, they certainly know who he is now.

There were shades of Shahid Afridi or Abdul Razzaq in the flamboyant nature of the way Razaullah flayed England to all parts.

He ended up needing to use three different bats at the crease after breaking two with his explosive hitting.

"It's the first time he's been out there for Pakistan ever, and he absolutely lights up the show. This is the attitude that was needed," said former Pakistan captain Ramiz Raja on BBC Test Match Special.

"Someone with a strong body language and who believes in himself. They'll want him playing all formats because he's a natural in mind, body language and attitude. It was a tremendous fightback."

At times when Razaullah - who has one first-class century - was teeing off, England captain Joe Root wore the expression of a chess player waiting for someone to tell him it was his move.

Root stationed eight fielders on the boundary at one point - but it did not deter Razaullah as he brashly swaggered at the crease with the arrogance of youth.

This was a special innings.

Razaullah's nine sixes is the joint-most ever in a Test innings in England. The other is Ben Stokes' famous 155 with nine against Australia in the Ashes Test in 2023.

He hit as many sixes as Sir Geoffrey Boycott did in his 108-Test career.

Perhaps being so far behind, and expected to capitulate, liberated Pakistan. There was a freedom to their batting hitherto unseen in this series so far.

Shan Masood played with admirable application with a stoic 95 while captain Babar Azam, a weight lifted off his shoulders, made 76.

Yet it was the swashbuckling Razaullah who really captured the imagination.

"England are going to win this Test match, I'm sure," said former England captain Michael Vaughan.

"But Razaullah has given Pakistan cricket some hope. They've unearthed a gem and he will be a superstar for many years."

Even Razaullah's dismissal was pure theatre lapped up by the crowd. Reprieved lbw to Dan Lawrence he danced down the pitch and was stumped next ball.

The young Pakastani left the field to the warmest ovation.

In another world he might have been playing for Cleethorpes in the Yorkshire Cricket Southern Premier League, having signed for the 2026 season only to be called up to a national training camp in May.

Those with tickets for Saturday must have thought the prospect of seeing any play was remote when Pakistan offered a meek surrender on day one.

Steamrolled for 133 just after lunch in Birmingham on Wednesday they looked rudderless against opponents who were ruthless.

Doubtless many punters will have started to make other plans in the expectation this would all be over swiftly, especially when England racked up 453.

Yet with 129 to defend, Pakistan have an outside chance of what would be the most famous of victories.

It's tempting to look at Pakistan cricket through a certain prism, but when moments like these arrive it's impossible not to. Through the emotional wringer again - despair to hope in the space of three days.

"There wouldn't be any person in the world that would've thought we'd go to day four," added Vaughan.

"That is what Pakistan cricket is. They have had a difficult few weeks. The team has been in turmoil. That is why I love Pakistan cricket.

"England will look back at a lot of the tactics and realise they got it wrong. The short stuff, one over of spin, the second new ball with the spinner.

"That day today will make the England team realise there is a long way to go to be world class."

articles.title: Joao Pedro: Chelsea boss Xabi Alonso says striker like Karim Benzema and as good as Erling Haaland
articles.text:
Xabi Alonso says Chelsea striker Joao Pedro is similar in style to his former Real Madrid team-mate Karim Benzema - and at a comparable level to Manchester City's Erling Haaland.

The Brazil international, 24, has scored twice and provided two assists in his first three games of the season - and was named the Premier League's Player of the Month on Friday.

It was the first time Joao Pedro has won the award as he finished ahead of team-mate Cole Palmer, who was Chelsea's previous recipient in September 2024.

When asked whether the forward could be compared to the prolific Haaland, who won last season's Premier League Golden Boot with 27 goals, Blues boss Alonso said: "I would say yes.

"If you count how many top strikers we have in the Premier League, I'm sure that Joao [Pedro] is there, Haaland for sure is there. So I would rate him that way."

Joao Pedro signed a new contract at Stamford Bridge last month to stay until 2034, and was handed Chelsea's number nine shirt at the start of the season.

He became the club's first striker since Diego Costa to score 20 goals in a single season during his debut campaign and has struck 25 times and had 11 assists in 57 matches since joining last summer.

In his last 57 matches for City, Norway's Haaland has 42 goals and supplied nine assists.

Unlike Haaland, who is a specialist goalscorer, Joao Pedro has played as a midfielder, number 10 and winger during his career and possesses a more rounded skillset.

Alonso, who made 195 appearances alongside former Ballon d'Or winner Benzema at Real Madrid, said there were also similarities between the Frenchman and Joao Pedro.

"In many things he reminds me of Benzema, because he is good in the box, he is good out of the box, he is good coming to his left side, he is good with the head, he is very complete, he is intelligent," added the Spaniard.

"So yes, he is still young, still things to develop, but many, many absolutely outstanding qualities that he has."

Benzema, now 38 and a free agent, has scored 523 goals in 994 appearances for France, Lyon, Real Madrid and Saudi Arabian sides Al-Ittihad and Al-Hilal.

Meanwhile, Joao Pedro was a surprise omission from Brazil's squad for the World Cup this summer, but has since been recalled for September's international fixtures against New Zealand and India.

Asked whether the omission by Brazil manager Carlo Ancelotti, who coached Alonso at Real Madrid, had provided added motivation this season, the Chelsea boss said: "He had enough motivation.

"He already had enough within him, so I didn't need to go there. It was painful for him, but that is in the past. We are now focused on what he is doing well and what he can do better.

"He has been outstanding. Not just in football terms, but in his personality, his maturity and his desire. He has a very clear goal this season, which is to have a great campaign and score a lot of goals."

articles.title: Solheim Cup 2026: Carlota Ciganda lifts Europe to a 4-4 tie with US on opening day
articles.text:
Carlota Ciganda once again stole the show after Europe's top pairing of Charley Hull and Lottie Woad failed to ignite against the USA on the opening day of the Solheim Cup.

The 36-year-old Spaniard - the oldest player competing this weekend - let out a roar after holing a 15-foot putt to earn Europe an unlikely half point in the final fourball match of the day and ensure honours are even at 4-4.

Ciganda's celebration evoked memories of the nerve-shredding finale at Finca Cortesin in 2023, when her putt allowed Europe to retain the trophy with a 14-14 tie.

And once again Nelly Korda, beaten by Ciganda in Spain three years ago, was on the receiving end.

The world number one and her playing partner Lauren Coughlin both left match-winning putts short to allow Ciganda, who had crucially won the 16th hole with an eagle, to deliver a stunning reprieve for Anna Nordqvist's team at Bernardus Golf Club in the Netherlands.

"I love this week. I just love playing for the team, for my team-mates. We fought hard and we got half a point, which is important," said Ciganda, who is playing in her eighth Solheim Cup.

"It gives us big momentum and hopefully we can take that into and win both [of Saturday's] morning and afternoon sessions."

European hopes of parity had begun to fade into the shadows of the evening sunshine, with Angela Stanford's visitors seemingly assuming control of the 20th edition of the biggest team competition in women's golf.

It proved to be a hard-fought opening day between Europe and a US team looking to retain the trophy following their 15½-12½ victory in Virginia two years ago.

However, despite Ciganda's heroics, there was also a sense of what might have been for the hosts, who found themselves 6-2 behind at this stage two years ago at the Robert Trent Jones Golf Club.

History has shown a good start to be essential in this competition, with the team holding the advantage after the opening day taking home the trophy 14 out of 19 times.

And the decision to send out Hull and Woad first in both the morning foursomes and the afternoon fourballs failed to deliver the impetus Europe's captain Nordqvist would have hoped for.

When Hull and rookie Woad emerged on the raucous opening tee with daylight barely breaking through at 06:40 BST, they did so as the two highest-ranked players in the European side at eight and seven respectively.

Yet despite winning the opening hole, Nordqvist's gamble never looked like paying off against the formidable pairing of Korda and Allisen Corpuz.

The American duo won all four of their foursomes matches across the previous two editions of this contest and became the first to make it five on the spin with a comfortable 4&3 victory.

Disappointingly for Europe, Hull and Woad then let a three-hole advantage slip on the back nine on Friday afternoon against Yealimi Noh and Angel Yin, who was playing only her third competitive round since June.

They did at least scramble a half point despite loud music being played by an on-course DJ clearly distracting Woad and Noh as they lined up their final putts. BBC Sport has contacted the Ladies European Tour about the incident which clouded the end of a pulsating match.

In contrast Europe's three other debutants, Julia Lopez Ramirez, Mimi Rhodes and Nastasia Nadaud, delivered in style.

England's Rhodes and France's Nadaud produced a superb performance to defeat Corpuz and Auston Kim 2&1, while the big-hitting Lopez Ramirez teamed up with her compatriot Ciganda in that final match against Korda and Lauren Coughlin.

"There's another 36 holes [on Saturday], so not every player's going to play five matches," said Nordqvist of her plans.

"Sometimes you've got to sit out someone, and for me, it was important to play all 12 players [on Friday], and the way the pairings worked out, that's how I had to play it."

During the build-up Nordqvist and Stanford both spoke of using the Solheim Cup as an advertisement for women's golf.

And the levels of skill, drama and grit on display only served to underline those comments, with the American players also poignantly wearing custom pins to commemorate the 25th anniversary of the 9/11 attacks.

"I just told them that I was proud of them again," said Stanford after the conclusion of play.

"We took a big swing from them. When you send Charley and Lottie out first, both sessions, we took some of their best body blows today.

"I'm excited because I feel like we're a heavyweight fighter. We fight with our mentality and we're just going to see how long we can last, and I feel pretty good about how long we can go."

Korda in particular set the tone early on Friday with her fifth win with Corpuz, equalling the points record for pairings set by Europe's Alison Nicholas and Laura Davies.

The US pairing of Alison Lee and Coughlin were always in control against Nanna Koerstz Madsen and Celine Boutier, taking their foursomes match 3&2 as the US opened a 2-0 lead.

An out of sorts Koerstz Madsen, who talked to her coach between sessions about her swing, and Boutier were also later on the end of a 5&3 demolition in an encounter that marked Megan Khang's sixth consecutive win in Solheim matches and her eighth in the past nine - this time alongside the metronomic Alison Lee.

Europe's fightback in the opening session was initiated by Swedish duo Maja Stark and Linn Grant who defeated Rose Zhang and Jennifer Kupcho 3&2.

Leona Maguire and Esther Henseleit followed that up by holding their nerve to defeat Andrea Lee and Lindy Duncan in another match that went down the 18th.

The victory meant Maguire improved her career Solheim Cup record to nine wins, three defeats and one halved match, to give her the highest winning percentage o any European player that has played five matches.

On Saturday, eight more points will be available across the foursomes (alternate shot) and fourballs formats, before the singles on Sunday, which will involve all 12 players on each team.

Europe require 14½ points to regain the cup, while US need 14 points to retain it.

articles.title: World Athletics Ultimate Championship: Armand Duplantis stars as sport's new global event begins
articles.text:
A bright pink sandpit and a pitch black infield. A brand new trophy and historic prize money.

The World Athletics Ultimate Championship is posed as something different in the sport, but some things stay the same - pole vault star Armand Duplantis taking centre stage.

As the inaugural competition's official song, which two-time Olympic champion Duplantis wrote and recorded, was played to a sell-out crowd of more than 20,000, all eyes fell on the Swedish 26-year-old as, yet again, it was just him against the world record.

Duplantis had already secured the title of inaugural champion in the event he has long dominated, and his $150,000 (£110,000) slice of the record $10m (£7.4m) prize pot on offer.

While he was unable to clear 6.32m and set the 16th world record of his remarkable career, an entertaining battle with Greek challenger Emmanouil Karalis had provided the blockbuster finale to the opening night of action in Budapest.

"I approached this event with a combination of a lot of nerves and excitement," said Duplantis.

"This was a missing piece for me to become the ultimate champion."

The condensed three-day format of the Ultimate Championship will see the world's best athletes go head-to-head across an innovative format which governing body World Athletics and its president Lord Coe hope can shape the sport's future.

Friday's upbeat curtain-raising session featured eight finals over three hours and brought victories for several global stars including Jakob Ingebrigtsen, Yaroslava Mahuchikh and Masai Russell.

Great Britain's Keely Hodgkinson, Georgia Hunter Bell, Amy Hunt and Matthew Hudson-Smith will be among those hoping to land the sport's newest global prize on Saturday.

As win percentages flashed up on screen, and sparklers lit up the dark backdrop as athletes posed with their trophies, athletics attempted to take its first steps in a brand new direction.

On Thursday, the world's top athletes had arrived for the championship at a red carpet event. On Friday, they emerged to light shows and dramatic music.

The appearance of the arena was immediately striking, with an infield painted black with the intention of directing the audience's focus to the illuminated live action.

On TV, augmented reality was used to display athlete headshots, win probabilities and projected finishing positions for each event.

For their crowning moment, athletes lifted their trophy from a plinth beside their competition area before heading to a winners' enclosure in the stands where they joined the likes of Usain Bolt and Noah Lyles.

The first to lift a trophy inside the stadium which hosted the World Championships three years ago was the United States' mixed 4x100m relay quartet, who shared $80,000 (£59,000) between them after winning in 39.64 seconds.

Great Britain's Romell Glave, Imani-Lara Lansiquot, Jeremiah Azu and Success Eduan finished third, behind Jamaica, in 40.26.

Jazmin Sawyers went close to producing a sensational end to the women's long jump - but she was still delighted to finish second at the end of a season which has brought Commonwealth gold and European silver.

The 32-year-old only returned from a devastating Achilles rupture on her take off leg last year but has quickly returned to career-best form and finished with a 6.78m leap.

"I really enjoyed it. I felt like I had a bit more in me but this competition was always a bonus for me," said Sawyers.

"I never thought I'd be here. I never thought, based on the first half of the season that I had, that I would be able to make top eight in the world."

articles.title: England vs Pakistan: Alastair Cook and Michael Vaughan question Joe Root tactics in Razaullah onslaught
articles.text:
England had "no plan" and were "out of control" in the face of Razaullah's stunning hitting on the third day of the final Test against Pakistan, according to former captain Alastair Cook.

Razaullah, the 21-year-old batting at number nine on Test debut, clobbered 81 from 63 balls at Edgbaston.

He shared a ninth-wicket partnership of 121 with Muhammad Abbas to drag the third Test into an unlikely fourth day, with England set 130 for victory.

Though the hosts are heavy favourites to earn a 3-0 clean sweep, the carnage of the final session was an alarming spell as Joe Root begins his second spell as captain.

Root's tactics were often criticised in his first spell as skipper and there were further questions of the Yorkshireman when he stood in for former captain Ben Stokes earlier this summer.

"You can get done by the tail - it's very hard when people have the license and ability to hit sixes," Cook told Test Match Special. "What I saw was no plan, it got out of control.

"That's when you need the backroom staff and coaches to step up. I would loved to have seen a message and some real leadership from the coaches."

England are currently led by interim head coach Marcus Trescothick, with New Zealander Stephen Fleming due to take on the role from December's tour of South Africa.

Trescothick is assisted by bowling coach Tim Southee, who was seen on the boundary rope at times during the partnership.

England's tactics were curious throughout the Razaullah-Abbas partnership. The seamers often stuck to a short-ball plan, with fielders back on the boundary. When their pace bowlers tried to hit the stumps, they could not find the target.

More bizarre was Root giving the second new-ball to part-time off-spinner Dan Lawrence, who had barely bowled in the series to that point. In doing so, Root bowled Lawrence in front of seamer Ollie Robinson, who has had a sensational summer as England's attack leader.

Jonathan Agnew, the former England fast bowler and the BBC's chief cricket commentator, called the tactics "appalling".

"You cannot and should not bowl like that to tailenders as soon as they come in," he said.

"You have to set the tone when you're bowling against tailenders. Yes, you bowl aggressively, but in a controlled way. They are numbers nine and 10 for a reason. It was bitterly disappointing.

"Dan Lawrence is a part-time off-spinner and he took the second new-ball. If you're looking for any aspect of the day that is utterly bonkers, that is it."

Razaullah's thrilling knock included nine sixes, tying the record for the most maximums in an innings by a batter on Test debut.

He also equalled Stokes' record for the most sixes in a Test played in England.

There were times when Root looked devoid of ideas, while the energy was sapped from his team. Jofra Archer cut a frustrated figure when Razaullah hit him for successive straight sixes and at one point Gus Atkinson was asked to bowl bouncers with eight fielders on the boundary.

"We shouldn't be surprised by England, they've delivered tactically like this on a regular basis," said ex-England captain Michael Vaughan.

"I think they'll win this game but they can't keep making mistakes like that. The basics of Test cricket generally work and that's to hit the top of the stumps. It's a bit of a warning sign that this attack is very good but they aren't the finished article just yet.

"Who are the characters in the team who are going got grab a hold of everyone and say, 'right, I'm going to make a moment'. I didn't see it from anyone today."

At one stage Root left the field for an opportunity to consult with the England backroom staff, although it did little to alter the course of the evening.

Eventually, Abbas poked the pace of Josh Tongue to point before Razaullah was stumped off Lawrence from the final ball of the day to leave Pakistan 453 all out.

"I'm disappointed, of course," said Trescothick. "We were in a position where they were eight down and the scores were level. We were hoping to go through them pretty quickly.

"We tried many different things. You have variations of plans. We bowled the short ball for a period of time, then length for a period of time, then a bit of spin. You're always chopping and changing, with various ideas.

"You'd always like to think you can do it better and you analyse it afterwards saying, 'right, was there an area or tactic we missed to get it right?' You hope in those situations when you bowl it in the right place, which we did on many occasions, that you get the nick or bowl them. Fair play, they played pretty well."

articles.title: Super League: Wigan 50-12 Catalans Dragons - Warriors win sixth League Leaders' Shield
articles.text:
Betfred Super League

Tries: Smith, Marshall 2, O'Neill, Farrell, Daniel, Field, Eckersley, Keighran Goals: Keighran 7

Tries: Tison, Lis Goals: Aispuro-Bichet, Garcia

Wigan Warriors won a sixth League Leaders' Shield as they ran in nine tries to beat Catalans Dragons and carry on their remarkable run of form heading into the Super League play-offs.

Matt Peet's side, who were trophyless in 2025 off the back of their quadruple-winning 2024 campaign, have now won two pieces of silverware, having lifted the Challenge Cup in May, and are now two games away from a treble.

Harry Smith and Ugo Tison exchanged tries early on, but Liam Marshall, Brad O'Neill and Liam Farrell put Wigan in control at the break.

Austin Daniel and Jai Field continued Wigan's scoring streak, while Zach Eckersley, Adam Keighran and Marshall's second wrapped up a thumping 16th win in a row, with Alexis Lis scoring a fine consolation try for Les Dracs in the closing stages.

Despite Friday's victory ensuring the shield was theirs, the really hard work was done in last week's crucial win over title rivals Leeds Rhinos at Headingley, where they leapfrogged their rivals to go top.

Had Wigan have lost then, Leeds could have pulled off a dramatic final-day surge back to the top, winning the shield at their expense on points difference, but the Rhinos fell short and were beaten by Hull FC on Friday.

Wigan now have a bye week by virtue of a top two place and will be at home for their Super League play-off semi-final on Saturday, 26 September, live on the BBC.

For Catalans, it means a difficult campaign ends with a ninth-placed finish. Les Dracs have now not made the end-of-season play-offs since their run to the Super League Grand Final in 2023 - where they were also beaten by Wigan.

For Wigan, winning the Shield is the culmination of a remarkable turnaround in form having been sixth in the table during a controversial and heavy 62-4 defeat away to Hull KR in May in the lead-up to the Challenge Cup final.

That defeat was their fifth in nine games, but since that point they have won all 16 games, beginning with their triumph at Wembley against the Robins.

There were tributes pre-match to captain Farrell, who announced he will retire at the end of the season, as Wigan's players warmed up with t-shirts emblazoned with Faz 12.

The hosts got off to the perfect start as Smith sold a perfect dummy to glide through the Catalans' defence to score, but that lead was cut back thanks to Tison's impressive solo effort soon after.

Marshall cantered in at the corner to put Wigan back ahead, while O'Neill spotted a gap to go through, and Farrell saw the half out having returned from a shoulder injury which had left him on the sidelines since June.

Daniel's easy run-in on the wing got Wigan going after the break before Field raced in from Farrell's offload to continue the rout.

Eckersley's 27th try of the season sent Wigan further ahead as he showed great intelligence to race through, while Keighran matched his fine work with the boot with a long-range run-in of his own. Marshall barged through for his second - leaving Farrell to take, and subsequently miss, the conversion.

Fellow retiree Ben Garcia did succeed with the boot, however, as he kicked the extras in the aftermath of Lis' try on the verge of the full-time hooter.

articles.title: Richarlison: Tottenham forward's move to Vasco da Gama falls through
articles.text:
Tottenham forward Richarlison's proposed move to Vasco da Gama has fallen through amid ongoing uncertainty over the Brazilian's future.

Sources have suggested Spurs had agreed a fee with Vasco over a return to Brazil for the 29-year-old.

However, personal terms over the deal are understood to have emerged as an issue.

The Brazilian transfer window closes on Friday night and there is an emerging sense Richarlison will stay at Spurs.

The attacker was left out of Tottenham's Premier League squad after his proposed £35m deadline-day move to Everton broke down over a disagreement on personal terms.

On Thursday, BBC Sport reported that Richarlison and Spurs were in a dispute over the remaining nine months on his contract.

Tottenham boss Roberto de Zerbi did not provide any update on Richarlison's future at a news conference earlier on Friday.

Richarlison is understood to be exploring his options, with sources indicating he is keen to be released from the remainder of his current deal, which runs out next summer - but Spurs can also trigger a 12-month extension.

The ex-Watford and Everton player was Tottenham's leading scorer in the Premier League last season with 11 goals to help the club avoid relegation.

"Richarlison is a good guy, a very good guy. I spoke with him a lot of times and I spent time to convince him to stay, but if you ask me, I know the truth," De Zerbi said.

"I know what happened in the last month, the last 45 days, and it's clear, but I'm not frustrated.

"If I had decided myself to leave him outside of the squad, I would have regrets, but the decision has not even been taken by the club. It has been a consequence of what I told you already that he has decided...

"I'm sorry because it could be different. Even the end of the story. It could have been better, or it was much better [with] Richarlison inside the list, happy to stay, maybe to extend his contract, because he is still an important player.

"He was important last season, we can't forget, but we can't forget also the last 45 days."

articles.title: English Open: Shaun Murphy beats Judd Trump in final-frame decider
articles.text:
Shaun Murphy snatched a thrilling final-frame victory over Judd Trump to reach the semi-finals of the English Open.

World number seven Murphy moved 5-4 ahead before Trump, the world number three, cleared 112 to take the match to a decider.

Murphy managed to overcome his English compatriot in a nervy final frame, helped by some deft safety play, to set up a semi-final against Mark Williams.

Williams withstood a fightback from fellow Welshman Liam Davies to book his spot in the semi-finals with a 6-3 victory.

Williams was level at 2-2 at the interval but pulled clear and eventually sealed his victory with a 112 clearance.

England's Kyren Wilson was left scoreless in the first three frames as Ding Junhui cruised to a 6-2 victory.

Wilson briefly threatened a comeback, winning the next two frames to reduce the deficit to 3-2, but China's Ding quickly regained control and took the final three frames to seal his place in the final four.

Ding will face Ali Carter in the semi-finals, who produced an excellent late display to edge past Zhou Yuelong 6-5 by winning three frames in a row.

Zhou had been leading 5-3, but Carter was able to turn it around from frame nine onwards, making the most of Zhou missing a routine yellow, then winning the next 80-39 before dominating in the decider.

Both semi-finals take place on Saturday, with Ding taking on Carter at 12:00 BST before Murphy faces Williams at 18:00.

articles.title: Garcia vs Benn: Conor Benn & Ryan Garcia both make weight for WBC title fight
articles.text:
Conor Benn and Ryan Garcia both comfortably made the welterweight limit for their WBC title fight despite concerns at how they would fare on the scales.

Briton Benn, 29, weighed in at 10st 6lb (66kg) for Saturday's bout - half a pound heavier than the champion.

The official weigh-in took place behind closed doors at the UFC Apex on Friday, in front of about 50 members of the media, before a ceremonial event later in the day which will be open to the public.

Garcia has won 25 of his 28 professional contests, including 20 knockout victories, with two defeats and one no-contest. Benn has 25 wins - 14 by knockout - and one loss, and is fighting for his first world title.

American Garcia, 28, won the WBC belt with a dominant points victory over Mario Barrios in February and is making his first defence against Benn.

Much of the build-up this week has centred on how Benn would cope with returning to the 10st 7lb welterweight limit for the first time in more than four years.

His two fights against Chris Eubank Jr were both at middleweight, with Benn weighing 11st 2lb (71kg) for the first and 11st 5lb (72kg) for the rematch. For his win over Regis Prograis in April, Benn weighed 10st 10lb (69kg).

He has already said he will vacate the title and move back up in weight if he beats Garcia.

Benn had looked increasingly gaunt and drawn during fight week and told BBC Sport the cut had taken him to the "pits of hell".

But Benn smiled as his weight was announced and looked in good shape, surprising several observers who had expected the effects of the cut to be far more visible.

A handful of undercard fighters weighed in after Benn while Garcia was still nowhere to be seen, prompting questions about whether the Californian was having difficulties making the limit.

Garcia has had problems on the scales before. He weighed more than three pounds over the light-welterweight limit before his fight against Devin Haney in 2024.

There was no such drama this time. Garcia sprinted towards the scales about 10 minutes after Benn and also looked at ease as he comfortably made weight.

articles.title: US Open tennis 2026 men’s semi-final: Ben Shelton defeats Frances Tiafoe in four sets – live reaction
articles.text:
Shelton is told that while Andy Roddick remains the last American man to win the title, he will become the first Black man to play in the US Open final since Arthur Ashe in 1972. “It’s a lot of emotion,” Shelton says. “My dad, my mom have sacrificed a lot for me to be in this position today. My dad lost his mom earlier this year, and she’s the reason that he was able to play tennis. Without her, there’s no Ben Shelton standing here today. So this one is for her. This one is for her.”

Shelton then turns his attention to Sunday and the Arthur Ashe Stadium crowd.

“I’m going for it here,” he says. “I’m gonna leave it all on the court. I hope you guys are coming back with me. Let’s do this for the USA.”

Before leaving the court, Shelton also acknowledged the significance of the date.

“It’s a difficult day to be out here playing,” he says. “My thoughts and prayers go out to all the families who were impacted by 9/11. This is one of the greatest, greatest cities in the world, and one of the biggest tragedies. Thoughts and prayers to everyone involved and affected.”

“[Frances] like a big brother to me, to be honest,” says Shelton in his on-court interview. “Every time that we get to take this court together, Arthur Ashe, and play each other is super special. But this is where we want to be, at the tail end of this tournament. This is both our favorite tournament in the world, our favorite court in the world, and to be able to light it up in front of you guys is the best feeling that there is.”

He’s asked what is different about the Ben Shelton of today compared to the one who reached his first US Open semi-final three years ago.

“I think I’ve grown up,” he says. “I’m more mature, more focused. I know what my goal is. I know what my job is out here,and I’m 100% committed to those goals.”

He continues: “It’s not easy playing here on Arthur Ashe. You’re playing in front of all your favorite athletes and movie stars, so to be able to keep your head down and focus for over three hours is not an easy task. I keep on looking up at the screen like, ‘Oh, shoot, Jalen Brunson’s here.’”

Shelton wins 4-6, 6-3, 6-3, 7-5!

Shelton breaks in 12th game of fourth set!

Fourth set: Tiafoe 6-4, 3-6, 3-6, 5-7 Shelton

Tiafoe blinks first in a muscular 10-shot exchange and suddenly he’s down love-15. He the nets a backhand on the run and it’s love-30. Shelton is two points from the finish line. Tiafoe then pushes Shelton out of position but can’t punish him, sending a forehand past the baseline for three match points. Shelton wastes the first, putting backhand into the net. And Tiafoe double-faults! Oh no! A terrible way to end this match. The players embrace at the net before Shelton points to his father and coach, saying: “This is our time.”

Updated at 23.14 EDT

Fourth set: *Tiafoe 6-4, 3-6, 3-6, 5-6 Shelton (*denotes next server)

A straightforward hold at 15 for Shelton and Tiafoe will serve to force a fourth-set tiebreaker after the change of ends.

Fourth set: Tiafoe 6-4, 3-6, 3-6, 5-5 Shelton* (*denotes next server)

Tiafoe opens with his third ace of the night, but misfires off the forehand side for 15-all. Tiafoe then gets lucky when a Shelton forehand caroms off the netcord forward, giving him a sitter to put away easily for 30-15. Shelton then sprays an inside-out forehand from the baseline into the alleyway, but Tiafoe does the same thing on the next point for 40-30. Game point ... and Tiafoe serves-and-volleys before putting away a forehand volley winner early in the point and letting out a scream to the heavens.

Fourth set: *Tiafoe 6-4, 3-6, 3-6, 4-5 Shelton (*denotes next server)

Tiafoe wins the first point on Shelton’s serve and the crowd buzzes. But Shelton peels off four staccato points to hold. Tiafoe will serve to stay in the tournament with Shelton four points from a first grand slam final. Squeaky-bum time inside Arthur Ashe Stadium!

Fourth set: Tiafoe 6-4, 3-6, 3-6, 4-4 Shelton* (*denotes next server)

That could have been a dangerous service game for Tiafoe, but he makes it easy on himself with another love hold. He’s won 11 of the last 12 points on his serve.

Fourth set: *Tiafoe 6-4, 3-6, 3-6, 3-4 Shelton (*denotes next server)

An even quicker hold at love for Shelton, who cracks four unreturnable serve to put the pressure back on Tiafoe.

Updated at 22.53 EDT

Fourth set: Tiafoe 6-4, 3-6, 3-6, 3-3 Shelton* (*denotes next server)

A brisk love hold for Tiafoe, who strikes his second ace of the match.

Fourth set: *Tiafoe 6-4, 3-6, 3-6, 2-3 Shelton (*denotes next server)

An imperious service game for Shelton, who holds at 15 after crunching his 16th, 17th and 18th aces of the night.

Fourth set: Tiafoe 6-4, 3-6, 3-6, 2-2 Shelton* (*denotes next server)

Tiafoe plays a couple of loose points and finds himself down love-30 facing a massive pressure point. An 18-shot rally ensues and Shelton’s airtight defense has Tiafoe in trouble ... but Tiafoe is able to hit a sensational lob winner! What surely looked like triple break point becomes 15-30. Phew! Tiafoe is able to escape from there. Incredible stuff!

Fourth set: *Tiafoe 6-4, 3-6, 3-6, 1-2 Shelton (*denotes next server)

Shelton holds comfortably, capping it with back-to-back aces down the middle of 133mph and 117mph.

Fourth set: Tiafoe 6-4, 3-6, 3-6, 1-1 Shelton* (*denotes next server)

Tiafoe makes his first double fault of the night, but otherwise strolls through an uncomplicated service game.

Updated at 22.23 EDT

Fourth set: *Tiafoe 6-4, 3-6, 3-6, 0-1 Shelton (*denotes next server)

Tiafoe went off court for a wardrobe change between sets, taking about eight minutes before play resumed in the fourth. It may have done him good. Shelton blinks first in an 18-shot rally then misses on a backhand for love-30. After hitting a backhand winner, he follows with a double fault for 15-40 and double break point. Tiafoe wastes the first with an unforced error off the backhand, then Shelton erases the second with a 140mph ace for deuce. Shelton then errs off the backhand for a third break-point chance, which he’s able to erase. Now Tiafoe raised a hand to stop play and Shelton serves anyway, thinking he won the point. Tiafoe disputes it, asking to replay the point. Both players approach the chair. Cooler heads prevail and the point is replayed. From there Shelton is able to serve himself out of trouble and hold to open the fourth. A 10-minute, 12-point gauntlet.

We’ve also learned there was a miscalculation by the speed gun during the last set and Shelton’s alleged record-breaking 158mph serve was actually somewhere in the mid-140s. Isner’s record is restored and safe.

Updated at 22.42 EDT

Shelton wins third set, 6-3!

Third set: Tiafoe 6-4, 3-6, 3-6 Shelton

Danger zone for Tiafoe, who makes a couple of unforced errors to go behind love-30 on his serve. He really won’t want Shelton serving first with a two-sets-to-one lead. He’s able to scratch back for 30-all, but Shelton wins the next exchange for 30-40 and set point. The full house swells. Shelton misses on a forehand early in the point for deuce. Shelton follows with a forehand winner for a second set point ... and he saves that one too after Tiafoe play a touch volley, then a lob, then an overhand smash for deuce. Tiafoe pounds a forehand winner for game point, Shelton answers with a backhand winner for another deuce. Now Tiafoe frames a forehand and it’s a third set point for Shelton in a game that’s gone more than nine minutes. And Shelton misses a forehand for deuce number four. Deuce number five. Deuce number six. Deuce number seven. And finally Shelton is able to stake a fourth set point ... and this time he converts! A marathon 20-point game spanning more than 15 minutes and Shelton snatches it to move within a set of his first grand slam final!

Third set: *Tiafoe 6-4, 3-6, 3-5 Shelton (*denotes next server)

Shelton holds at love, crushing his 11th and 12th aces of the night. Tiafoe will serve to stay in the third set.

Third set: Tiafoe 6-4, 3-6, 3-4 Shelton* (*denotes next server)

Tiafoe holds at love. Much-needed. Shelton had won 10 of the previous 11 points before that game.

Third set: *Tiafoe 6-4, 3-6, 2-4 Shelton (*denotes next server)

Shelton strolls through his service game to consolidate the break.

Shelton breaks in fifth game of third set!

Third set: Tiafoe 6-4, 3-6, 2-3 Shelton* (*denotes next server)

Another scratchy service game for Tiafoe and he’s quickly down love-40, gifting Shelton three break-point chances. And he needs only one! Shelton rips a cross-court backhand winner to finish off a 10-shot rally and secure the break for his first lead of the night.

Third set: *Tiafoe 6-4, 3-6, 2-2 Shelton (*denotes next server)

With Shelton serving at 15-all, he casually steps up and pounds a 158mph serve out wide, which would be the fastest ever recorded serve at an ATP event, besting the previous mark of 157.2 mph set by John Isner at the 2016 Davis Cup. Well then. He gets to 40-15 before Tiafoe pushes it to deuce. But Shelton wins two quick points from there to nail down the hold.

Updated at 22.17 EDT

Third set: Tiafoe 6-4, 3-6, 2-1 Shelton* (*denotes next server)

The nerves creep in for Tiafoe, who hits a couple of scratchy forehands and suddenly finds himself 15-40 and double break point down. He’s made to work to save the first one, getting the best of a 31-shot rally from the baseline, the longest exchange of the night. He then saves the second on a quick point for deuce. Tiafoe wins another 21-shot point to move within a point of the hold and Shelton is going to approach the chair umpire to complain that Tiafoe is going past the serve clock. It’s been three straight points for Tiafoe where the clock has elapsed past zero and there’s yet to be a warning given. We’ll see what comes of that. Tiafoe then wins the next point to hold, winning four on the trot from 15-40 down.

Third set: *Tiafoe 6-4, 3-6, 1-1 Shelton (*denotes next server)

And Shelton answers with an easy hold of his own, pounding his 10th ace of the night along the way, a 132mph missile down the middle.

Third set: Tiafoe 6-4, 3-6, 1-0 Shelton* (*denotes next server)

Stress-free hold for Tiafoe to open the third set.

Updated at 21.37 EDT

Shelton wins second set, 6-3!

Second set: Tiafoe 6-4, 3-6 Shelton

Shelton doesn’t fool around, rattling off three quick points for triple set point. He squanders the first despite battering Tiafoe back with a 149mph serve, but Tiafoe nets a return on the next one. Shelton takes set two after 34 minutes.

Shelton breaks in eighth game of second set!

Second set: Tiafoe 6-4, 3-5 Shelton* (*denotes next server)

With Tiafoe serving at 15-30, a sensational 17-shot rally ensues which the older American finally caps with a highlight-reel backhand winner. It’s 30-all. But Shelton follows with a backhand winner for 30-40 and break point ... and he converts it when Tiafoe errs off the forehand side! Shelton pumps a fist and plays to the crowd and will serve for the second set!

Updated at 21.01 EDT

Second set: *Tiafoe 6-4, 3-4 Shelton (*denotes next server)

Shelton falls behind love-15, but reels four quick unreturnable serves: 125mph, 144mph, 139mph, 140mph. It’s a hold and they’re still on serve in the second.

Second set: Tiafoe 6-4, 3-3 Shelton* (*denotes next server)

Another drama-free hold for Tiafoe, who’s won eight of nine points on his serve since getting broken at love.

Second set: *Tiafoe 6-4, 2-3 Shelton (*denotes next server)

An emphatic service game for Shelton, who holds at love to stay on serve.

Updated at 20.55 EDT

Second set: Tiafoe 6-4, 2-2 Shelton* (*denotes next server)

Tiafoe backs up the break comfortably. We’ve just hit the hour mark in what could be a long night.

Tiafoe breaks in third game of second set!

Second set: *Tiafoe 6-4, 1-2 Shelton (*denotes next server)

Now it’s Shelton who buckles on his serve. He misfires a backhand for love-15, then sees Tiafoe pound consecutive winners for love-40 and triple break point. Shelton is able to save the first, but he makes another unforced error off the backhand to gift the break right back. We’re back on serve in the second.

Shelton breaks in second game of second set!

Second set: Tiafoe 6-4, 0-2 Shelton* (*denotes next server)

Well, well, well. Tiafoe’s first serve goes into full revolt as Shelton is able to break at love to take the upper hand early in the second.

Second set: *Tiafoe 6-4, 0-1 Shelton (*denotes next server)

Shelton shakes it off and holds comfortably to open the second set.

Updated at 20.36 EDT

In case you missed it, Taylor Townsend is a US Open champion at last. The 30-year-old American teamed with Kateřina Siniaková to win the women’s doubles title on Friday, adding a home grand slam crown to a career that has included years of setbacks, scrutiny and perseverance. Our Andrew Lawrence with the report:

double quotation markThe cheers swelled from Arthur Ashe Stadium as Taylor Townsend approached the microphone on court. “Y’all know this is my moment,” she started, “and I’m about to take it.”

A day after being denied an American rooting interest in the women’s singles final and rushing for the exits in response, the Ashe crowd had reason to stick around and drink in the moment: the Chicago native and her partner, Kateřina Siniaková of the Czech Republic, had just defeated the all-American team of Ashlyn Krueger and Robin Montgomery 5-7, 6-0, 6-2 in Friday’s women’s doubles final. With the victory, Siniaková became a two-time career doubles slam champion while Townsend joined the club for the first time.

Tiafoe wins first set, 6-4!

First set: Tiafoe 6-4 Shelton

No fuss, no muss. Tiafoe holds at love for the first time all night and he’s closed out the opening set in 45 minutes.

Updated at 20.38 EDT

Tiafoe breaks in ninth game of first set!

First set: *Tiafoe 5-4 Shelton (*denotes next server)

Shelton gets to 30-love on his serve but a relentless Tiafoe pushed it to deuce. The crowd swells. Shelton then misfires with the forehand and it’s a second break point of the night for Tiafoe. And Shelton double-faults! Oh dear! Tiafoe has the first break of the night and will serve for the opening set!

First set: Tiafoe 4-4 Shelton* (*denotes next server)

Tiafoe is pushed to 30-all on his serve, but he follows with a forehand winner then a backhand volley winner to cap a nine-shot rally for 4-all. A tightly wound start before this electric atmosphere on Ashe. Who will blink first?

First set: *Tiafoe 3-4 Shelton (*denotes next server)

Shelton makes his first double fault of the night, but rattles off four quick points for the elementary hold. Still on serve in the opening set.

First set: Tiafoe 3-3 Shelton* (*denotes next server)

Tiafoe holds from love-15. A very clean start for the 28-year-old with only two unforced errors in the first six games.

First set: *Tiafoe 2-3 Shelton (*denotes next server)

Shelton holds from love-15 then 15-30. Promising sign for the younger American: he’s gotten 17 of 19 first serves in (89%).

First set: Tiafoe 2-2 Shelton* (*denotes next server)

A bit of pressure on Tiafoe now as he goes down 15-30 on his serve. But he gets it to 30-all with a gorgeous angled volley at the net that Shelton can’t recover. Tiafoe then gets the better of a 13-shot exchange for game point before capping the hold with a crisp forehand winner.

Updated at 20.02 EDT

First set: *Tiafoe 1-2 Shelton (*denotes next server)

Shortly after crunching his first ace of the night, 123mph down the middle, Shelton faces his first pressure point of the night at 30-all. He then makes an unforced error off the backhand for 30-40 and will face his first break point, but he rattles off three quick points from there to escape with the hold.

First set: Tiafoe 1-1 Shelton* (*denotes next server)

Tiafoe answers with an easy hold of his own. It’s a gorgeous night here in Queens: 76F (24C) with a light breeze.

First set: *Tiafoe 0-1 Shelton (*denotes next server)

Shelton holds at 15, getting four of five first serves in. It must be noted how dialed-in this capacity crowd is tonight. None of the ambient din of non-stop conversation were so used to hearing in here.

The players have finished their warm-up. Shelton has elected to serve first. We should be under way any moment now. There’s barely an empty seat in 23,771-seat Arthur Ashe Stadium.

Before the players emerge tonight, Arthur Ashe Stadium is pausing to mark the 25th anniversary of the September 11 attacks. A pre-match ceremony is honoring the nearly 3,000 people killed, their families and the first responders. After a moment of silence, the recording artist JoJo is performing the US national anthem.

Updated at 19.37 EDT

Shelton is attempting to become the youngest American man to reach a US Open final since Andy Roddick won the title here at 21 in 2003. The 23-year-old has been remarkably efficient when reaching the business end of tournaments this season: he has made four previous semi-finals – Dallas, Munich, Stuttgart and Montreal – and won the title every time. Those trophies also made him the first American man since Sam Querrey in 2010 to win tour titles on hard, clay and grass in the same season. Tonight he will go for five finals from five semi-final appearances.

Updated at 19.30 EDT

If tonight’s match turns into another war of attrition, both men appeared seasoned for the task. Tiafoe has already spent 16hr 3min on court across five matches, the fourth-longest journey to a US Open semi-final since the ATP began tracking match times in 1991. Shelton is only slightly fresher at 15hr 41min. Tiafoe has played 19 sets and Shelton 20, with both coming through five-set quarter-finals. The difference is down to literal mileage: Shelton has covered 44,143ft during the tournament to Tiafoe’s 39,472ft.

A strong US Open for the American juniors is heading into the final weekend, with four US players – two boys and two girls – through to championship matches on Saturday.

Seventeen-year-old Marcel Latak of Darien, Illinois, has a chance at a rare double after reaching the boys’ singles and doubles finals. He wil face Brazil’s Luis Guto Miguel, the junior world No 1 and top seed, for the singles title before teaming with fellow American Tanishk Konduri, also 17, against France’s Aaron Gabet and Spain’s Valentin Gonzalez-Galino in the doubles final.

Latak is bidding to become the first American to sweep the singles and doubles titles at a grand slam since Robin Montgomery did it at the 2021 US Open.

On the girls’ side, California sisters Kristina and Annika Penickova, aged 17 and 16 respectively, have reached the doubles final, where they will face Polina Berezina and Alisa Terentyeva.

All four junior finals are scheduled for Saturday.

Hello and welcome to Arthur Ashe Stadium for tonight’s all-American US Open men’s semi-final between Frances Tiafoe and Ben Shelton. For the third time in four years, the two friends and crowd favorites will meet at Flushing Meadows. Shelton won their first New York encounter, overpowering Tiafoe in four sets in the 2023 quarter-finals on his way to a breakthrough semi-final appearance at 20. Tiafoe answered 12 months later, coming from two sets to one down to win a five-set thriller in the third round. Shelton leads their overall series 3-1, including a straight-sets victory in Washington last summer.

Tonight’s rubber match is considerably bigger. The winner will become the first Black American man to reach the US Open singles final since Arthur Ashe in 1972 and the first to reach any grand slam singles final since MaliVai Washington at Wimbledon in 1996. He will also become only the fifth American man this century to reach the final in New York, after Pete Sampras, Andre Agassi, Andy Roddick and Taylor Fritz.

Both men arrive after extraordinary five-set quarter-finals. Tiafoe somehow escaped Alex Michelsen after trailing by two sets, falling a break behind in the third and then going 3-0 down in the fifth. His 5-7, 3-6, 7-5, 6-3, 7-6 (6) victory put him into his third US Open semi-final in five years, matching Agassi for the most by an American man this century.

Shelton’s route was even more spectacular. The 23-year-old toppled defending champion Carlos Alcaraz 6-7 (5), 6-1, 6-3, 1-6, 7-6 (7) in a late-night classic that finished at 3.33am, ending the Spaniard’s 18-match winning streak at grand slam level and securing his first victory over a top-three opponent after starting his career 0-17 against them.

One American dream ends tonight and another moves into Sunday’s final against Alexander Zverev with a shot of ending the country’s 23-year wait for a men’s major champion.

The first ball will not be at 7pm local time as scheduled while Ashe changes over for the separately ticketed night session. We’ll update you with an approximate start time as we hear.

articles.title: ‘This is my moment’: Taylor Townsend’s road comes full circle with US Open triumph
articles.text:
The cheers swelled from Arthur Ashe Stadium as Taylor Townsend approached the microphone on court. “Y’all know this is my moment,” she started, “and I’m about to take it.”

A day after being denied an American rooting interest in the women’s singles final and rushing for the exits in response, the Ashe crowd had reason to stick around and drink in the moment: the Chicago native and her partner, Kateřina Siniaková of the Czech Republic, had just defeated the all-American team of Ashlyn Krueger and Robin Montgomery 5-7, 6-0, 6-2 in Friday’s women’s doubles final. With the victory, Siniaková became a two-time career doubles slam champion while Townsend joined the club for the first time.

The moment was long in coming for the 30-year-old Townsend, a top-ranked junior player who was body-shamed by her home federation and denied coaching and funding as consequence. Last year, Townsend and Siniaková blitzed through the draw before getting blitzed back by Gabriela Dabrowski and Erin Routliffe, pushing her US Open victory celebration back a year. Though clearly disappointed, Townsend maintained a sunny disposition and vowed that she and Siniaková would finish the job. That they did in a year when the US Open showcased the depth of Black American players in tennis wasn’t lost on Townsend – who now has an adult US Open trophy to go with the one she won as a 16-year-old.

In many ways, the US Open has been the through-line for Townsend’s meandering story arc. Her junior doubles title here in 2012 – on the heels of a doubles title at Wimbledon and doubles and singles titles at the Australian Open – stamped her as a star on the rise, the crafty leftie charging down the hard trail blazed by the Williams sisters. Also during that US Open, Townsend became a national story when her mother revealed that the USTA had pulled funding for her trip and that the family had passed the plate around to get her to New York.

“I wasn’t in 100% health, and I said, I’m going to come, and I’m going to do what I can,” she recalled in press afterward. “To be able to come here and win as an adult, you know, and be able to play on Arthur Ashe and to hold this trophy, it’s something that’s so special to me, because I don’t forget the things that I’ve gone through.”

When Townsend’s pro career struggled to meet expectations, her physique became the default target for criticism; Pat McEnroe, then USTA’s player development chief and still a prominent narrator at this tournament, set the tone by effectively pronouncing Townsend physically unfit for federation support. The knock-on effects of that decision were undeniable: Townsend sank from 94th in the world singles rankings to 304th and hustled to remain on tour in the absence of sponsorship support, essentially playing tournaments for gas money. At the 2016 US Open, Townsend scrapped to qualify for the main draw – only to wind up losing her first-round match to fallen former world no1 Caroline Wozniacki.

The story could have ended there. But Townsend persevered, cracking the top 100 again in 2017 before reemerging in the US Open spotlight. In 2019, she gritted her way through qualifying again and stormed to the fourth round of the main draw, scoring her first top-10 victory against Simona Halep before losing to eventual winner Bianca Andreescu and ending the year a career-high 73rd in the rankings. When it appeared as if becoming a mom in 2021 might slow her down, she used it as motivation to get into the best shape of her life.

It all snapped into focus. In 2024, Townsend stopped the presses with a maiden doubles slam victory at Wimbledon, then kicked off the next year by winning doubles at the Australian Open. But it was the US Open that served as the main stage for Townsend’s breakout again as she made another fairy tale run to the fourth round in singles and battered the nostalgia act of Venus Williams and Leyla Fernandez en route to the doubles finals – where she and Siniaková lost in straight sets.

They eventually bounced back, with Townsend helping the team to a noteworthy, for an American, championship on the terre battue of Roland Garros in June before making a triumphant return to New York as the people’s champ. She rallied the crowd behind her tassely outfits and indefatigable exuberance for another fourth-round singles run (losing to top-seeded Aryna Sabalenka this time) before completing her doubles revenge tour with Siniaková – a partnership that began with an Instagram direct message. (“I always say it: Guys, don’t be afraid to slide in the DMs,” Townsend joked.) On a sun-splashed Friday afternoon at Ashe, Montgomery and Krueger put a brief scare into Townsend and Siniaková, breaking for the first set. But the top-ranked doubles team quickly shook that off; in the second set shutout, they’d concede just two points on serve before cruising to the finish.

Basking in the afterglow of victory, Townsend resurfaced in the interview room at Ashe with another tassley outfit on and a gold grill in her mouth while double-fisting a pair of Honey Deuces – one more than she brought to the table last year. It was a hard-earned moment to gloat for a player who had been written off from the start. And she didn’t let the moment pass without acknowledging just what an achievement it was to reach this career peak as so many of her Black American contemporaries were making deep tournament runs. As on court, she made a point of uplifting Montgomery, a doubles wildcard entrant who qualified for the singles main draw.

“I’m so proud to be able to click on the TV and watch Frances [Tiafoe] and Ben [Shelton],” she said. “One of them is going to be able to be in a Grand Slam final, and that’s a beautiful thing. You know, Robin, myself, you know, it’s been Coco [Gauff], it’s been a phenomenal US Open for people of color, and just being able to show people, like, it’s possible, you know?”
